thread:
oncall-bot: Handoff summary for UTC shift ending now. Primary: Maria I. -> handing to Devon K. Secondary: Sasha L. stays on as backup. Brief: we had two customer-facing incidents (latency spike for hosted api and a node OOM in dedicated pool). No P0s open now but still monitoring. Links: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-4321 :eyes:
Maria I.: quick notes on the OOM: one worker node hit OOM at 01:14 UTC, kube evicted the pod; autoscaler didn't spin a replacement fast enough. Pod logs show repeated allocation spikes from model kv cache load. We mitigated by lowering max_prefetch and bumped autoscale_min to 2.
Devon K.: got it. Who should I page if we see high tail latency again? runtime-oncall or infra?
Maria I.: routing rules in runbook. Short answer: if 5min rolling latency > 2s and request queue is growing -> page runtime-oncall. If node-level failures / OOM / scheduling -> page infra-oncall. If it's auth failures or cert issues -> security-oncall. If customers are calling -> loop in Lee (support).
Sasha L.: adding the runbook snippet here for quick copy:
```
# Handoff playbook excerpt
if latency_spike and queue_growth:
  page runtime-oncall
elif pod_eviction or node_oom:
  page infra-oncall
elif suspicious_data_exfil or creds_leak:
  page security-oncall and legal
else:
  notify support and watch
```
Also see: /runbooks/oncall-routing.md (internal).
Lee (support): FYI - we already opened a support ticket for the latency spike (TS-9988). We sent an initial note to the customer at 02:04 UTC. If we hit another customer-visible spike, escalate to exec-comms.
Paging-Bot: Reminder: to page oncall use `/page runtime-oncall (incident summary)` or `/page infra-oncall (incident summary)`. Use `!escalate` to ping primary+pager duty.
Devon K.: there's a small coverage gap 23:00-01:00 PST where infra-oncall is rotating. Who covers infra overnight?
Maria I.: infra has partial coverage — their primary is on call but not in the US overnight. If infra doesn't ack in 10m, page infra-secondary and ping Sasha. We also set automatic fallback in routing: route to dedicated fallback model (lower memory) for hosted customers if runtime can't allocate.
Sasha L.: I'll add an inline pointer in the runbook to the fallback model and the kube commands we used. Quick commands used during mitigation:
```
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/model-serving
kubectl top nodes
# to lower max prefetch
kubectl set env deploy/model-serving MAX_PREFETCH=16
```
Devon K.: thanks. Also, question about security routing: if we suspect a token leak from logs (s3 presigned urls in traces), do we page security immediately or gather more evidence?
Security-Oncall: page security immediately and use the incident channel `#sec-incident` for coordination. Treat as potentially PII/credentials exposure. Preserve logs, do not rotate keys before triage unless instructed. Legal will join if confirmed.
Maria I.: handoff checklist for Devon:
- Review INC-4321 notes and runbook links above
- Check autoscaler and node counts in cluster A (us-west-2)
- Watch latency dashboards for next 4 hours (alert threshold lowered to 1.5s temporarily)
- If infra doesn't respond in 10m to pages, escalate to Sasha + use infra-secondary channel
- Customer comms: coordinate with Lee before sending substantive updates
Devon K.: acked. I will be primary from now until 14:00 UTC. I'll post status updates in this thread for any pages.
Maria I.: leaving monitoring to you — ping me if you need a hand. Thanks for picking up. :thumbsup:
Devon K.: quick note — I saw an elevated 503 rate from a single availability zone at 02:30 UTC. I'm going to run the affinity check and maybe shift traffic away. If that causes capacity issues, I'll fall back to the lower-memory model routing.
Sasha L.: good plan. If you need to reroute, remember to update routing-policy A/B entry and run `routectl promote fallback-model --reason "oom mitigation"`.
Devon K.: doing it now.
Paging-Bot: New page sent to runtime-oncall.
Devon K.: update: routed ~20% traffic away from az-3 -> error rate decreased to baseline in 3m. Keeping an eye.
Lee (support): Noted. I'll hold on external updates until we see a stable 30m window.
Security-Oncall: no evidence of data exposure from the logs we saw. Will continue monitoring.
Maria I.: final: Devon, there is a known gap for on-prem dedicated customers between 04:00-06:00 UTC where Private-team is thin. If anything touches private stack, escalate to product-support + infra.
Devon K.: got it. I'll add a note on the incident page and tag private-team. Thread will remain open for the next 6 hours for follow-ups.
oncall-bot: Handoff recorded: primary now Devon K., secondary Sasha L., handoff complete. :white_check_mark:
